text:
lucas: Quick thought from maintenance: what if we publish a tiny `redwood-lite` that only includes request/streaming primitives (no oauth/faraday) for tiny sampleapps and CLIs? Could reduce onboarding friction a lot.

anya: Love the idea. We keep the main `redwood` as the full gem, and `redwood-lite` for constrained envs. How do we avoid duplicating code and diverging behavior?

rui: We can extract common code into a shared internal gem `redwood-core` and have both `redwood` and `redwood-lite` depend on it. `redwood` pulls auth + extras. `redwood-lite` stays minimal.

jamie: Parity concern: streaming retry + auth coupling. Right now token refresh is in the same call stack as the stream loop. If we split, core must surface a refresh hook so `redwood-auth` can subscribe. Otherwise we risk subtle differences in reconnect behavior.

lucas: Exactly. Proposal: core exposes a hook interface `Redwood::Hooks.on_before_stream_retry(&block)` and the auth gem registers a refresher. Then `redwood-lite` simply doesn't register anything.

anya: Can you sketch the API? Also worth adding a small section in Quickstart showing `gem install redwood-lite` for minimal examples. Many community users on Windows/Lambda hit bundler conflicts because they install full gem for simple usage.

rui: API sketch:```ruby
module Redwood
  module Hooks
    def self.on_before_stream_retry(&blk)
      @before_stream_retry = blk
    end

    def self.call_before_stream_retry(context)
      @before_stream_retry&.call(context)
    end
  end
end
```

jamie: Nice. For backwards compatibility, we can keep the existing monolith gem but mark it deprecated after one major. Add a compatibility shim that requires both core and auth for a transition period.

dev-bot: ci: ruby-3.1 matrix job #902 failed: bundler could not resolve dependency tree. Log: "In snapshot: faraday (= 2.0.0) In Gemfile: some-plugin (~> 1.2) depends on faraday (~> 1.8)"

lucas: That's the exact friction. `redwood-lite` should not depend on faraday/oauth2. Keep HTTP client layer minimal and let consumers plug adapters.

anya: Action items I'd suggest: 1) Draft RFC describing split and transition plan, 2) Create `redwood-core` as internal gem, 3) Publish `redwood-lite` alpha and update Quickstart, 4) Add CI job that tests core-only installation and sampleapp, 5) Add a small test that ensures streaming behavior remains identical with and without auth hook.

rui: I'll spin up the core gem repo and add the hook API. I can also add a CI matrix entry that installs `redwood-core` only.

jamie: I'll write the Quickstart patch to show both `redwood-lite` and `redwood` installs and include a troubleshooting note about bundler conflicts. Also will review the RFC.

lucas: One more: let's add a tiny migration note in CHANGELOG and a deprecation policy. No rush to force people to migrate.

anya: +1 to the plan. Also ping ops/security about signing keys for publishing a new gem org if needed.

dev-bot: reminder: link to draft issue template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/issues/764 (stub)

lucas: OK I'll open the RFC as a draft PR and tag folks. Thanks all.
